draft.title: Physical activity guidelines
card: Australia's physical activity guidelines say how much activity each age group needs for good health. They are set by the Australian Government's Department of Health.
Children and young people
For ages 5 to 17, the guidelines say at least 60 minutes a day of moderate to vigorous activity. Vigorous activity and muscle and bone strengthening should be included on at least three days a week.
Adults

For ages 18 to 64, the guidelines say to be active on most days, with at least 2.5 to 5 hours of moderate activity a week, or an equal amount of vigorous activity. Muscle strengthening should be included on at least two days a week.
Sitting
Every age group is also told to limit sedentary time, and to break up long periods of sitting. For young people, this includes keeping recreational screen time to no more than two hours a day.
draft.remember: The guidelines set a minimum amount of activity for each age group, and they also tell people to limit sitting.

a.q: Which advice is part of Australia's guidelines for a 15-year-old?
opts: At least 60 minutes of moderate to vigorous activity a day
At least 30 minutes of light activity on most days
At least 60 minutes of vigorous activity every day
At least 2.5 hours of moderate activity a week
a.why: For ages 5 to 17, the guidelines say at least 60 minutes a day of moderate to vigorous activity. The 2.5 hours a week is the adult minimum, so it does not fit a 15-year-old.
a.clue: Think about which age group 15 falls into.

b.q: Leo, 16, plays sport for 70 minutes every day and then spends five hours a night on recreational screens. How does he compare with the guidelines?
opts: He meets the activity advice but not the sitting advice
He meets both the activity advice and the sitting advice
He meets the sitting advice but not the activity advice
He meets neither, because 70 minutes is too much activity
b.why: Seventy minutes a day is more than the 60 minute minimum, so he meets the activity advice. The guidelines also say to limit sitting, including recreational screen time, so five hours of screens does not meet that advice. Being active does not cancel out the sitting.
b.clue: The guidelines give two separate pieces of advice, so check each one.

a.best: At least 60 minutes of moderate to vigorous activity a day

b.best: He meets the activity advice but not the sitting advice

problems.detail: "At least 2.5 to 5 hours of moderate activity a week" is muddled. The guideline is to accumulate 2.5 to 5 hours (150 to 300 minutes) of moderate activity, or 1.25 to 2.5 hours of vigorous activity, a week. Pairing "at least" with a range confuses the minimum. Suggest: "2.5 to 5 hours of moderate activity a week (at least 2.5 hours)".

The federal department was renamed the Department of Health, Disability and Ageing in 2025, so "Department of Health" may be out of date for a 2025 course. Consider "the Australian Government's health department".
